summary.name: VeraCrypt
summary.one_liner: VeraCrypt is free, open-source disk encryption software for Windows, macOS and Linux that encrypts files containers, partitions and drives on the fly.
keywords: open source encryption windows mac linux
use_cases: Creating an encrypted virtual disk inside a file
Encrypting a USB flash drive or external hard drive
Encrypting the Windows system partition with pre-boot authentication
Hiding encrypted data with a hidden volume
Migrating existing TrueCrypt containers to VeraCrypt format
summary.what_it_does: VeraCrypt creates an encrypted virtual disk within a file and mounts it as a real disk. It can also encrypt an entire partition or storage device such as a USB drive or hard drive, including the partition where Windows is installed, using pre-boot authentication. Encryption is automatic, real-time and transparent, and the page says it can be hardware-accelerated on modern processors. It supports hidden volumes and a hidden operating system for plausible deniability. It can load TrueCrypt volumes and convert TrueCrypt containers and non-system partitions to VeraCrypt format.
notable: Based on TrueCrypt 7.1a, with stronger key derivation: 200000 default iterations for system encryption and 500000 for containers and other partitions
Hidden volume and hidden operating system for plausible deniability
Files are PGP-signed and SHA256/SHA512 checksums are published
Can convert and load TrueCrypt containers
caveats: Opening encrypted volumes takes extra time because of the higher iteration counts, as the page itself notes
The page lists release updates through 2026 but gives no details on platform support beyond the named OSes
